summary:
I've been building a Japanese-learning app for myself, and the most interesting bug this month was in a comprehension quiz: I had it flag the right answer by showing four English options where only one matched a question mark or "isn't" in the sentence. Turned out you could get 88% of items right without reading a word of Japanese — the English distractors were leaking the answer through punctuation. Flipping it to show Japanese answer tiles against an English cue took the solvable-without-reading rate to zero, and I wrote a test that scores the same items using only the English glosses, specifically so a broken detector can't just report a clean number and be wrong.

I also generate the app's artwork through ComfyUI, running two open models on a home GPU. The useful lesson was about how to fix bad output: banning a prop (an apron, a leash) doesn't work — the model just re-attaches the same trope somewhere else, three tries running. Removing the prop from the scene works. And with one of the models, which has no negative-prompt slot, saying "no holes" in the prompt draws holes — you have to describe the blank surface you actually want instead of naming what to avoid.

Separately, I run a small broker service (Switchboard) that lets one shared GPU serve several different models — a chat model, an image generator, a speech model — without them fighting each other for memory. It queues requests and evicts whichever model isn't in use, so from the outside it looks like there's more hardware than there really is.

The other fix worth mentioning was a mobile UI bug that looked like a routing problem and wasn't. A user reported that tapping one button opened a completely different screen. I checked the backend logic, the view model, the deployed code — all correct. The actual cause was two adjacent buttons 35px tall with a 7px gap between them, below Apple's 44px minimum, so a thumb aimed at one reliably landed on its neighbor. I measured it properly (sampling tap points outward from the button's center) instead of guessing from a screenshot, and the fix was to remove the second button entirely rather than make it bigger.

highlights.oneLiner: Generating app artwork on a home GPU; learned removing a prop beats banning it in the prompt.
Broker service queuing one shared GPU across chat, image, and speech models.
